courseTitle: Ionic - Build iOS, Android & Web Apps with Ionic & Angular

cues.en: To show that map modal,
we already made our first step,
we can now call then and get our modal element here which we can of course present,
so modal el present like this and this will open our map modal component in a new modal.
With that, let's go to the map modal component and
let's make sure we get something onto the screen there. In the map modal component,
I will add an ion-header, I didn't add that to the location picker because that will be a component I
use inside of other components, the map modal component on the other hand should render like a single
page even though it's enclosed in a modal. I want to have a toolbar in there and I'll add a title and
there, I will say pick location and I'll add some buttons here with ion-buttons like this and you see
I'm getting a bunch of errors here.
The reason is that in the shared module where I declared the map modal, I'm not importing the Ionic
module which actually unlocks all these Ionic components,
so make sure to add the Ionic module import from @ionic/angular to the shared module
and with that added, you'll see that all these errors will magically go away since that unlocks all these
Ionic components.
So now back to the buttons, in the toolbar, I'll add ion-buttons with a slot of primary to add them
on the right side typically and then, I'll add a button here which will actually say cancel so that when
we open that modal to pick a location, we can tap on the map to pick a location or we click the cancel
button to get out of there
and of course for that, I'll add a click listener here and call onCancel.
Now after that, I'll add my ion-content here and inside of the ion-content, I'll add a simple div
which I will actually use to render my map
and for that, I'll give that a class of map and also a local reference of map by which I can later select it
in my Typescript code to interact with that div and render the map there.
So let me go back to the map modal component then and first of all, I'll add the onCancel handler here
which is triggered when we click the cancel button in our toolbar and there, I want to close the modal.
Now to close that, I need to inject the modal controller here as well,
so let's do just that,
let's add the modal controller, import it from @ionic/angular to the map modal component and in onCancel,
we can then use this to call dismiss and dismiss this modal here.
With that, we got everything to open the modal and dismiss it but we're not displaying a map.
Let's preview this nonetheless
and to preview this, we just need to make sure we include the location picker component here with the
app location picker selector in our form,
so in the new offer page here and for that
in the new offer module, I will import that shared module,
that's the idea of having the shared module,
so that now I can use the picker and also the modal if I want to in this component and make sure you have
the right path here which should be a relative path. Now in the new offer page here, I'll add a new
row and a new column of course and that column will receive the same size classes as my other
columns to be in line with them,
so let me add that there and then inside of this ion-column, we can add the app location picker, just
like that. With that, we should be able to see that button, so
let's go back to our application here and let's create a new offer and here's our button and if I tap it, indeed
that modal opens but of course there is no map in there, so time to finally render that.
